safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قال) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", i.e. Nūḥ, according to the apparent sense (اركبوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (فيها) as the previous one [Note: In the previous āya (40).], attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اركبوا) by its implying the meaning of "enter" (باسم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) [Note: The preposition may be attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of اركبوا, i.e. "saying" or "seeking blessing by the name of Allah"; in that case مجرى is parsed as an adverb of time or place attached to the ḥāl, or it is an adverb of time only with the intention of an omission, as you say جئتك مقدم الحاج, i.e. at the time of his arrival.. or it is a ḥāl if it is a mīmī maṣdar, as in our saying آتيك خفوق النجم. This analysis applies to (مرسى) because it is conjoined to it.], (الله) the Word of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (مجرى) postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (مرساها) like مجراها, and maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ربّ) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) (غفور) the khabar of inna, nominative (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «اركبوا فيها ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «باسم الله مجراها ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (فيها).
The clause «إنّ ربّي لغفور ...» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.

* Morphology:
(باسم): written in the Muṣḥaf with the hamzat al-waṣl dropped (بسم), whereas the orthographic rule is not to drop it, because dropping the hamzat al-waṣl happens only in the complete basmala (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم); but if you say باسم الله آكل or باسم الله أركب, there is no dropping.
(مجرى): noun of time or place from the trilateral verb جرى, its pattern being مَفْعَل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; it is also a mīmī maṣdar from the same verb with the same pattern, because the verb is weak-final (muʿtall nāqiṣ).
(مرسى): noun of time or place from the quadrilateral verb أرسى, its pattern being مُفْعَل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn; or it is a mīmī maṣdar from the same verb, with the same pattern.

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (هي) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (تجري) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil (agent) is "it" (هي) (الباء) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent (في موج) a preposition and its genitive noun, a second ḥāl from the agent of تجري (كالجبال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of موج (الواو) conjunction not indicating sequence (نادى) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif (نوح) fāʿil, nominative (ابن) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) parenthetical [Note: Or circumstantial, the clause then being in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(2, 3) In āya (40) of this sūra.], (كان) defective past verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (في معزل) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of kāna (يا) vocative particle (بنيّ) the one addressed, a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa, and (الياء), dropped for lightness, is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (اركب) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you" (معنا) like معه «2», attached to (اركب), (الواو) conjunction (لا) prohibitive, putting into the jussive (تكن) defective imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and its noun is a latent pronoun, implied as "you" (مع) like the previous one «3», attached to the khabar of تكن (الكافرين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «هي تجري ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: The (الواو) may be the wāw of ḥāl, the clause then being in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from something implied, i.e.: they embarked and set off while it was sailing.].
The clause «تجري ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هي.
The clause «نادى ...» is conjoined to the clause هي تجري.
The clause «كان في معزل ...» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
The clause «يا بنيّ ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted saying, i.e. نادى يقول يا بني [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, as an explication of the calling in His saying: نادى نوح ابنه.. See āya (22) of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.].
The clause «اركب معنا ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «لا تكن مع الكافرين ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the reply to the vocative.

* Morphology:
(معزل): noun of place from the trilateral عزل, of the ضرب class, its pattern being مَفْعِل with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, because its ʿayn is with kasra in the imperfect.
(بنيّ): it is the diminutive of ابن; originally it had three yāʾs: the first the yāʾ of the diminutive, the second the lām of the word – or its ʿayn according to the original – and the third the yāʾ of the first person; then the yāʾ of the first person was dropped for lightness and the yāʾ of the diminutive was assimilated into the lām of the word.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", i.e. Nūḥ's son (السين) particle of the future (آوي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "I" (إلى جبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آوي), (يعصمني) imperfect verb, nominative.. and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya) and (الياء) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "it" (من الماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعصم), (قال) like the first, and the fāʿil is "he", i.e. Nūḥ (لا) the lā of generic negation (عاصم) the noun of lā, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative (اليوم) adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أمر الله [Note: (عاصم) cannot be what governs اليوم, since if it were so it would have taken tanwīn.. Some allowed attaching (اليوم) to the khabar of lā, and al-ʿUkbarī rejected it.], (من أمر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar (predicate) of lā (الله) the Word of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (إلّا) particle of exception (من) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as an excepted, the exception being connected (muttaṣil) or disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) according to how the meaning of عاصم is interpreted [Note: On the connected reading: i.e. there is no protector except Allah; on the disconnected reading: i.e. but whoever Allah has mercy on is protected; and (عاصم) may mean "protected" (maʿṣūm), so the exception is connected.], (رحم) past verb, and the fāʿil is "He", i.e. Allah [Note: The object of (رحم) is omitted, and it is the referring pronoun (al-ʿāʾid).] (الواو) conjunction (حال) past verb (بين) adverb of place, accusative, attached to (حال), and (هما) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (الموج) fāʿil, nominative (الفاء) conjunction (كان) defective past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (من المغرقين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of kāna.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «سآوي ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يعصمني ...» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of جبل.
The clause «قال (the second) ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لا عاصم.. من أمر الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «رحم ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «حال.. الموج ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كان من المغرقين ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause حال.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(الر): disconnected letters (ḥurūf muqaṭṭaʿa) with no grammatical position [Note: See the first verse of Sūrat al-Baqara.]; (كتاب) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "this Qurʾān"; (أحكمت) a passive past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine; (آيات) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of القرآن (أحكمت) a passive past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine; (آيات) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Translator's note: the source text repeats a stretch here, apparently a copying error: "a pronoun in the position of القرآن (أحكمت) … (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive"; translated as written.]; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (فصّلت) like «أحكمت», and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya"; (من) a preposition; (لدن) a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فصّلت) or to (أحكمت) [Note: It may be attached to an omitted second khabar of the mubtadaʾ «هذا», just as it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب».]; (حكيم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (خبير) badal (substitute) from «حكيم» or a naʿt of it, genitive.
The clause «(هذا..) كتاب..» has no grammatical position; initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «أحكمت آياته ...» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of «كتاب».
The clause «فصّلت ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause «أحكمت».

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted: ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ خَبِيرٍ. لدن: it is an adverb (ẓarf) meaning «عند». Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī and Ibn Hishām set out the difference between the two, and we shall clarify that in what follows:
1- What al-ʿUkbarī says:
It is indeclinable despite occurring as a muḍāf, because the reason for its indeclinability is its departure from its counterpart; for «لدن» means «عند», but it (that is, «لدن») is specific to adjacency to the thing and very close proximity to it, whereas «عند» is not so; rather it is for what is near and what is far from it, and it conveys the sense of possession.
2- What Ibn Hishām says:
Two words alternate with «عند» (and "alternate" means resemble it and come close to it in meaning), namely:
«لدى» "without restriction", as in the saying of the Exalted: إِذِ الْقُلُوبُ لَدَى الْحَناجِرِ كاظِمِينَ and the saying of the Exalted: وَأَلْفَيا سَيِّدَها لَدَى الْبابِ.
And «لدن», which is used when the place is a place of the beginning of an extent, as in «جئت من لدنه» ("I came from his presence"). The two have come together in the saying of the Exalted: آتَيْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا وَعَلَّمْناهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا عِلْماً, for «عند» and «لدن» have come together in this verse. «لدن» differs from «عند» in that its being put in the genitive by «من» is more frequent than its being in the accusative, so much so that it never occurs in the Revelation in the accusative, whereas «عند» is often put in the genitive [Translator's note: so in the source.]. As for «لدى», its being put in the genitive is impossible. There is another difference, which is that «عند» and «لدى» are declinable (muʿrab) while «لدن» is indeclinable in the dialect of most. Likewise «لدن» may be annexed to a clause, unlike «عند» and «لدى», as in the saying of al-Quṭāmī:
صريع غوان راقهنّ ورقنه ... لدن شبّ حتى شاب سود الذوائب
(Felled by fair maidens who delighted him and whom he delighted, from when he grew into youth until his black locks turned grey.)

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative [Note: Or it is lightened from the heavy (inna), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and (لا) is a prohibitive lā making the verb jussive, and the clause is the khabar of the lightened «أن»; in that case it is orthographically preferable to write it separately (أن لا).. Or it is a particle of explanation (tafsīr) — and that is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān.]; (لا) negating [Note: or prohibitive, making the verb jussive, in the case where (أن) is lightened from the heavy one, or explicative.]; (تعبدوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), its sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent); (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الله) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تعبدوا..) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e., «بألّا تعبدوا» or «لئلّا تعبدوا».. attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «فصّلت» [Note: Some have permitted the interpreted maṣdar to be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "hiya".. and Abū Ḥayyān rejected that.].
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to «نذير»; (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to «نذير» [Note: The pronoun refers back to the Book.. And it may be attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) — a naʿt (adjective) placed before the noun it qualifies — and the pronoun then refers back to the Name of Majesty or to the Book.]; (نذير) khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (بشير) conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw to «نذير», nominative like it.
The clause «تعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative [Note: Or it is explicative, (أن) being preceded by the verb «فصّلت», which contains the sense of saying without its letters; and this is more apparent because it needs no implied element.].
The clause «إنّني.. نذير» has no grammatical position; it is in the status of a causal clause (taʿlīliyya) or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (أن) like the previous one [Note: in the previous verse (2).]; (استغفروا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent); (ربّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ثمّ) a conjunction; (توبوا) like «استغفروا»; (إلى) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (توبوا); (يمتّع) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the response to the request, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he", i.e., Allah; (متاعا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for its original maṣdar (verbal noun) «تمتيع», accusative; (حسنا) a naʿt (adjective) of «متاع», accusative; (إلى أجل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb «يمتّعكم»; (مسمّى) a naʿt of «أجل», genitive (majrūr), its sign of the genitive being an implied (muqaddar) kasra; (الواو) conjunction; (يؤت) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (يمتّع), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is "he"; (كلّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ذي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (فضل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (فضله) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن استغفروا) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تعبدوا).
(الواو) resumptive; (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (تولّوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, from which one of the two tāʾs has been dropped, its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna; (أخاف) an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is "I"; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أخاف) [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of «عذاب» — a naʿt placed before the noun it qualifies.]; (عذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (كبير) a naʿt of «يوم», genitive.
The clause «استغفروا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن) [Note: or conjoined to the explicative clause in the previous verse, if (أن) is parsed as explicative.].
The clause «توبوا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «استغفروا».
The clause «يمتّعكم ...» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e.: «إن تتوبوا يمتّعكم».
The clause «يؤت ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «يمتّعكم».
The clause «تولّوا» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «إنّي أخاف ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أخاف ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (مرجع) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction [Note: Or it is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause after it is a ḥāl of the Name of Majesty, its governor being the [implied] "being settled" (al-istiqrār).]; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «قدير»; (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (قدير) khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The clause «إلى الله مرجعكم..» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «هو.. قدير» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:81-83.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا يا لوط) is like قالوا يا صالح [Note: In verse (62) of this sura.], (إنّا رسل) is like إنّا.. [Note: In verse (70) of this sura.].. and (رسل) is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ [Translator's note: the source writes أنّ; the particle in the verse is إنّ.], nominative (marfūʿ); (ربّك) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لن) a particle of negation and naṣb; (يصلوا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the naṣb being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يصلوا); (الفاء) a conjunction linking the effect to the cause; (أسر) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is "you" (أنت); (بأهلك) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسر).. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بقطع) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسر); (من الليل) preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of قطع; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā, making jussive; (يلتفت) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (أحد), the fāʿil of يلتفت, nominative; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (امرأتك) excepted, accusative [Note: The exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), whether the thing excepted from is (أهل) or (أحد). Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr: "... the exception was not intended to exclude her — i.e. his wife — from those commanded to be taken away by night, nor from those forbidden to look back, so in that case the accusative would have been obligatory, as the only view." End quote; i.e. the exception here is munqaṭiʿ.].. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the noun of inna; (مصيب) a fronted khabar, and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi [Note: Or it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the relative noun after it is the khabar.]; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, a postponed mubtadaʾ; (أصاب) past verb, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "he" (هو), which is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (إنّ) like the first; (موعدهم) noun of inna, accusative.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الصبح) khabar of inna, nominative; (الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); (ليس) defective past verb; (الصبح) noun of laysa, nominative; (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (قريب) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of laysa.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative يا لوط ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّا رسل ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «لن يصلوا إليك» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the response to the vocative [Note: The clause of the response to the vocative came, in meaning, as a justification for the clause لن يصلوا إليك, so it is like a preparation for a badal (substitute); thus the clause may be a badal from the response to the vocative.].
The clause «أسر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumed clause, i.e. "Take heed, and travel by night (فأسر) ...".
The clause «لا يلتفت منكم أحد» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أسر ...
The clause «إنّه مصيبها ما ...» has no grammatical position: a justification of the exception.
The clause «مصيبها ما أصابهم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «إنّ موعدهم الصبح» has no grammatical position: an explicative resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أليس الصبح بقريب» has no grammatical position: resumptive — or parenthetical.
(فلمّا جاء أمرنا) its i'rab has passed [Note: In verse (66) of this sura.]; (جعلنا) past verb and its fāʿil; (عالي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (ها) is muḍāf ilayhi; (سافل) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (ها) is like the last; (الواو) conjunction; (أمطرنا) like جعلنا; (على) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أمطر) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of "We sent down" or "We let fall"; (حجارة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من سجّيل) preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt of حجارة; (منضود) a naʿt of سجّيل, genitive.
The clause «جاء أمرنا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the conditional with its protasis and apodosis is conjoined to the resumptive clause قالوا.
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أمطرنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
(مسوّمة) ḥāl, accusative, from حجارة [Note: It is valid for the ḥāl to come from حجارة because it has been described.. and it may be a naʿt.]; (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to (مسوّمة); (ربّك) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl; (ما) negating, operating like laysa; (هي) detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, the noun of mā; (من الظالمين) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بعيد; (الباء) a redundant preposition; (بعيد) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of mā.
The clause «ما هي ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from حجارة [Note: The clause may be cut off as resumptive, so it would have no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(أسر): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, in keeping with the indeclinable (imperative) form; its imperfect is يسري, and in it the hamza that is dropped in the imperfect returns; its past is أسرى.. its pattern is أفع.
(قطع): a noun meaning half the night, because a portion of it equals the rest..
And see verse (27) of Sūrat Yūnus.
(مصيب): active participle of the quadriliteral أصاب, its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.. The word contains iʿlāl by vowel-lessening (taskīn) and iʿlāl by substitution (qalb).. As for the taskīn, it is in making the weak letter vowelless and transferring its vowel to the ṣād before it; its origin is مصيب — with kasra on the yāʾ — and it became مصيب — with kasra on the ṣād and sukūn on the yāʾ.
And the iʿlāl by qalb is the changing of the wāw — since it is from الصواب — into yāʾ because it is vowelless and preceded by a kasra; the origin مصوب was transferred to مصيب.
(الصبح): a noun for the known, fixed time, extending until before sunrise.
(سافل): active participle of سفل يسفل, of the bāb of naṣara, the bāb of fariḥa and the bāb of karuma; its pattern is فاعل, and it is the low part of a building or a city.
(سجّيل): a concrete (jāmid) noun denoting an entity, meaning dried clay; its pattern is فعّيل with kasra on the fāʾ and the doubled ʿayn.
(منضود): passive participle of the triliteral نضد, its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Irsāl al-mathal, or tamthīl (coining a proverb): in the words of Allah the Exalted «أَلَيْسَ الصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ». It is a device that can be defined as: what the speaker utters becoming current in the way of proverbs that circulate [Translator's note: the source has الأفعال السائرة ("circulating acts"), evidently for الأمثال السائرة ("circulating proverbs").].

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(ألا) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (إنّهم) like «إنّي» [Note: in verse (3) of this sūra.]; (يثنون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent); (صدور) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (يستخفوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām, its sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil; (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يستخفوا), and the pronoun refers back to Allah.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يستخفوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يثنون).
(ألا) like the first; (حين) an adverb (ẓarf), accusative, attached to (يعلم) [Note: al-Zamakhsharī attached the adverb to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "they want concealment when they cover themselves..", so that it does not entail restricting His knowledge, Exalted is He, of their secret and their open to this particular time. Abū al-Baqāʾ attached the adverb to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "they conceal themselves", and to the verb «يعلم». Abū Ḥayyān and others attached it to the verb «يعلم», because there is no need for an implied element, since there is no ambiguity in the meaning.]; (يستغشون ثيابهم) like «يثنون صدورهم»; (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he"; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi [Note: or it is a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is mafʿūl bihi.], and the resumptive pronoun is omitted; (يسرّون) like «يثنون»; (الواو) conjunction; (ما يعلنون) like «ما يسرّون» and conjoined to it; (إنّه) like «إنّي» [Note: in verse 3 of this sūra.]; (عليم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (بذات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «عليم»; (الصدور) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «إنّهم يثنون ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يثنون ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna.
The clause «يستخفوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يستغشون ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يعلم ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يسرّون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (ما), whether nominal or particle.
The clause «يعلنون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «إنّه عليم ...» has no grammatical position; causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(يثنون): it contains a vowel-weakening by quiescence (iʿlāl bi-l-taskīn) and a weakening by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); its original form is «يثنيون» with ḍamma on both yāʾs; the ḍamma on the second yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent and its vowel was transferred to the nūn — weakening by quiescence — then the yāʾ was deleted because it met, while quiescent, the wāw of the plural — weakening by deletion; its pattern is يفعون.
(يستخفوا): it contains a weakening by quiescence and a weakening by deletion, following the course of «يثنون» ... its pattern is يستفعون [Translator's note: so in the source; the form in the verse is without nūn.].
(يستغشون): it contains a weakening by quiescence and a weakening by deletion, following the course of «يثنون»; its pattern is يستفعون.
(ثياب): plural of «ثوب», a primitive (jāmid) noun meaning clothing; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn, and the pattern of «ثياب» is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ.
Part Twelve
Remainder of Sūrat Hūd
From verse 6 to verse 123; Sūrat Yūsuf from verse 1 to verse 52

safi-cedvel:84-86.t:
* I'rab:
(وإلى مدين ... إله غيره) the i'rab of its parallel has passed [Note: In verse (50) of this sura.. And see verse (85) of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.]; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā, making jussive; (تنقصوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jazm being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (المكيال) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (الميزان) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to المكيال, accusative; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna; (أراكم) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is "I" (أنا).. and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (بخير) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi — or a ḥāl (circumstantial); (الواو) conjunction; (إنّي أخاف) like إنّي أرى; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أخاف); (عذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (محيط) a naʿt (adjective) of يوم, genitive.
The clause «(أرسلنا) إلى مدين ...» is conjoined to the clause (أرسلنا) mentioned in the context of the stories of the prophets mentioned earlier [Note: In verse (50) of this sura.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explicative resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «ما لكم من إله ...» has no grammatical position: justificatory (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا تنقصوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اعبدوا.
The clause «إنّي أراكم ...» has no grammatical position: justificatory.
The clause «أراكم بخير ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of (the first) inna.
The clause «إنّي أخاف ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّي أراكم.
The clause «أخاف عليكم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of (the second) inna.
(الواو) conjunction; (يا قوم) its i'rab has passed [Note: In verse (50) of this sura.]; (أوفوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (المكيال) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الميزان) conjoined to المكيال by the wāw, accusative; (بالقسط) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أوفوا; (الواو) conjunction; (لا تبخسوا الناس) like ولا تنقصوا المكيال; (أشياءهم) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (لا تعثوا) like لا تنقصوا; (في الأرض) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تعثوا); (مفسدين) a ḥāl confirming the content of the clause, accusative, the sign of the naṣb being the yāʾ.
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the previous clause يا قوم.
The clause «أوفوا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا تبخسوا الناس ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا تعثوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
(بقيّة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (خير) khabar, nominative; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to خير; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) defective past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) is a pronoun, the noun of kāna; (مؤمنين) khabar of kāna, accusative, the sign of the naṣb being the yāʾ; (الواو) conjunction; (ما أنا عليكم بحفيظ) like ما هي من الظالمين ببعيد [Note: In verse (83) of this sura.].
The clause «بقيّة الله خير» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «إن كنتم مؤمنين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are believers, then what remains from Allah is better for you"; so the good is conditional on faith.
The clause «ما أنا.. بحفيظ» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause إن كنتم مؤمنين.

* Morphology:
(المكيال): noun of instrument from the transitive triliteral كال, its pattern is مفعال with kasra on the mīm.
(بقيّة): it is written in the Muṣḥaf with the open tāʾ (بقيت), and nothing else in the Qurʾān is written that way [Translator's note: this is the author's claim as written.].

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (takrār): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَيا قَوْمِ أَوْفُوا الْمِكْيالَ وَالْمِيزانَ بِالْقِسْطِ».
Repetition occurs in this story in three ways, because He said "and do not diminish the measure and the scale" (ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان), and this is exactly the first, and there is nothing in it except the expression "and do not defraud people of their things" (تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم). Its benefit is that, since the people persisted in that ugly practice, forbidding them from it required exaggeration in emphasis, and repetition conveys intense concern with the matter. They were first forbidden the ugly thing they were doing, namely diminishing the measure and the scale; then the command to give full measure came, stated explicitly in its own word, so that it would be more stirring toward it and more inviting to desire for it.

safi-cedvel:87-87.t:
* I'rab:
«قالوا يا شعيب» is like قالوا يا صالح [Note: In verse (62) of this sura.]; (الهمزة) for the sarcastic interrogative; (صلاتك) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (تأمرك) imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is "she/it" (هي); (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle of naṣb; (نترك) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is "we" (نحن); (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi; (يعبد) like تأمر; (آباؤنا) fāʿil, nominative.. and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أو) a conjunction; (أن نفعل) like أن نترك; (في أموالنا) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نفعل).. and (نا) is like the last; (ما) like the first; (نشاء) like تأمر, and the fāʿil is "we".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نترك) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being تأمر [Note: Or in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition attached to (تأمر), i.e. تأمرك بأن نترك.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نفعل..) is in the position of accusative — or genitive — conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
(إنّك) is like إنّي [Note: In verse (84) of this sura.]; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (أنت) detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; (الحليم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الرشيد) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يا شعيب ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أصلاتك تأمرك ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «تأمرك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ صلاتك.
The clause «نترك» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يعبد آباؤنا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «نفعل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «نشاء» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «إنك لأنت الحليم» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «أنت الحليم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of (إنّك).

* Morphology:
(شعيب): a proper name, its pattern is فعيل in the form of the diminutive [Translator's note: the source has التصفير, evidently a misprint for التصغير "diminutive".], which is among the patterns most proper to names, and therefore it is declined as a triptote.

* Benefits:
- A sound opinion on the i'rab of (أن نفعل):
Allah the Exalted said in this verse أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ فِي أَمْوالِنا ما نَشؤُا. What first comes to mind is conjoining (أَنْ نَفْعَلَ) to (أَنْ نَتْرُكَ), and that is false, because he did not command them to do with their wealth as they please; rather it is conjoined to ما, so it is governed by "leaving", and the meaning is "that we leave doing ...". Yes, whoever reads تفعل and تشاء with tāʾ, not nūn, then the conjunction is to أن نترك. What gives rise to the mentioned misconception is that the parser sees أن with the verb twice, with a conjunction between them.
Abu al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī confirmed this same i'rab, saying: (أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ) is in the position of accusative, conjoined to ما يعبد, and the implied sense is "Does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worship, or that we leave doing ...", and it is not conjoined to أن نترك, since the meaning is not "Does your prayer command you that we do with our wealth".

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قيل) past verb, passive (أرض) the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative (يا) vocative particle [Translator's note: the source lists (يا) after (أرض); the order is kept.] (ابلعي) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الياء) an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent) (ماءك) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (يا سماء أقلعي) like يا أرض ابلعي (الواو) conjunction (غيض) like قيل, (الماء) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (الواو) conjunction (قضي الأمر) like غيض الماء (الواو) conjunction (استوت) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents.. and the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the fāʿil is "it", i.e. the Ark (على الجوديّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استوت), (الواو) conjunction (قيل) like the first (بعدا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. ابعدوا or بعدوا, by way of imprecation (للقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the maṣdar (بعدا) [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said: The lām in (للقوم) belongs to the complement of the maṣdar; a group disallowed attaching it to the maṣdar and said it is attached to His saying (قيل), the implied meaning being: and it was said for the sake of the wrongdoers, since one who has perished cannot be addressed except figuratively. Someone else said: it is for specification and clarification, attached to (قيل).. And it was said: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted, its implied form being "the imprecation", i.e. the imprecation is against the wrongdoing people.. so there are two clauses in the construction..
(2, 3) Because it is originally the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).. The majority make the nāʾib fāʿil omitted, its implied form being (القول), and the clause explicative.], (الظالمين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يا أرض ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil «2».
The clause «ابلعي ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «يا سماء ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يا أرض.
The clause «أقلعي ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the second vocative.
The clause «غيض الماء ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قضي الأمر ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «استوت على الجوديّ» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قيل (the second) ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «(بعد) بعدا..» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil «3».

* Morphology:
(غيض): in it the alif reverts to yāʾ and the first radical (fāʾ) of the word takes kasra
to suit the yāʾ.
(استوت): in it there is a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by dropping because of the meeting of two quiescents: the alif came quiescent before the tāʾ of the feminine and was dropped; its pattern is افتعت.
(الجوديّ): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for a specific mountain; and it is said: every mountain is called a jūdī.
(بعدا): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb بعد يبعد, of the كرم class, its pattern being فُعْل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- This noble āya is examined from four angles: from the angle of the science of bayān and from the angle of the science of maʿānī – these two being the foundations of rhetoric – and from the angle of eloquence of meaning and the angle of eloquence of wording. As for examining it from the angle of the science of bayān, which is examining the majāz (figurative usage), the istiʿāra (metaphor) and the kināya (metonymy) in it, and what is connected with that of the qarīna (contextual indicator), the tarshīḥ (reinforcement of the metaphor) and the taʿrīḍ (allusion): when He, mighty is His dominion, wanted to build the meaning: "We wanted to return what had burst forth from the earth to its belly, so it returned; and to cut off the deluge of the sky, so it was cut off; and to make the water that came down from the sky abate, so it abated; and to accomplish the affair of Nūḥ, peace be upon him – which is fulfilling what We had promised him of drowning his people – so it was accomplished; and to settle the Ark on al-Jūdī, so it settled; and We left the wrongdoers drowned," He, glory be to Him, built the speech on likening the thing intended with this to one commanded, from whom disobedience is impossible – because of the perfect awe in which he holds the commander – and on likening the bringing into being of what is intended to a decisive command, effective in bringing about what is sought, as a depiction of His immense power, glory be to Him, and that these immense bodies of the heavens and the earth follow His will, the Exalted, in bringing into existence and annihilating, and follow His wish concerning them in alteration and change, as if they were rational, discerning beings. Then upon the combination of the two similes He built the composition of the speech, and He, majestic and exalted, said: «قيل ...» as a majāz for will, of the type of mentioning the effect and intending the cause, because will is a cause of the occurrence of speech in general; and He made the qarīna of this majāz the addressing of inanimate things, namely «يا أرض ...» «ويا سماء ...»; and this address to the earth and the sky is by way of istiʿāra, because of the mentioned resemblance. What appears is that he [Translator's note: the author being drawn upon, unnamed here] meant there is an istiʿāra bi-l-kināya (implicit metaphor) here, since the thing likened is mentioned (I mean the sky and the earth, from which the occurrence of a matter is intended) and what it is likened to is intended (I mean the one commanded who is described as being incapable of disobedience, by way of claim), with the qarīna being the attribution of the address to it and the entry of the vocative particle upon it – both of these being properties of the obedient one commanded – and this would be a takhyīl (imaginative attribution). Then for the sinking of water into the earth He borrowed "swallowing", which is the action of drawing food in, because of the resemblance between them, namely going to a hidden resting place.
In al-Kashshāf: "swallowing" is made a metaphor for the earth's soaking up of the water, and this is better, because soaking up indicates a drawing by the parts of the earth of what is on it, like swallowing in relation to an animal, and because soaking up is the action of the earth while sinking is the action of the water, together with the correspondence (ṭibāq) between the two verbs in transitivity. Then He borrowed "water" for food by way of istiʿāra bi-l-kināya, likening it to food, because the earth gains strength through water in growing crops and trees as the eater gains strength through food; and He made the qarīna of the metaphor the word «ابلعي ...», because it is coined for use with food and not with water.
Then He, majestic and exalted, said: «ماءك ...», annexing the water to the earth, by way of majāz, likening the connection of the water with the earth to the connection of property with the owner; and He chose the pronoun of address for the sake of tarshīḥ. Its upshot is that there is a linguistic majāz in the annexation form that indicates possessive specification, and for this reason the address was made a tarshīḥ for this metaphor, in that the address indicates the earth's fitness for ownership.
Then for the withholding of the rain He chose "desisting" (iqlāʿ), which is an agent's leaving off an action, because of the resemblance between them in the cessation of what there was of rain or action; so in «أقلعي ...» there is an istiʿāra with respect to its substance, and likewise with respect to its form as well. It is built on likening the bringing into being of what is intended to a decisive, effective command, and the address in it is also a tarshīḥ of the metaphor of the vocative.
Then He, glory be to Him, said «وَغِيضَ الْماءُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْداً ...»
So He, majestic and exalted, did not state explicitly who made the water abate, nor who accomplished the affair, settled the Ark and said "away with". Likewise He, glory be to Him, did not state explicitly the one who said «يا أَرْضُ ...» «وَيا سَماءُ ...» at the beginning of the āya, following in each of these the path of kināya, because those immense matters issue only from One possessed of power whose essence cannot be fathomed, an Overpowering One who cannot be overcome; so there is no room for the imagination to go to someone other than Him, majestic is His greatness, being the one saying «يا أَرْضُ ...» and «يا سَماءُ ...», nor the one making abate what abated, nor the one accomplishing such a dreadful affair, nor that the settling and fixing of the Ark could be by the settling of anyone else.
Then He, the Exalted, sealed the speech with taʿrīḍ, as a warning to those who tread the path of those people in denying the messengers, peace be upon them, wronging only themselves and nothing else; and as a display of the place of displeasure and of the respect in which they deserved it, and that the rising of the deluge and that dreadful scene were only because of their wrongdoing, as the imprecation of destruction after their destruction announces, and the description with wrongdoing together with the ruling being tied to it.
As for examining it from the angle of the science of maʿānī, which is examining the benefit of each word in it and the reason for each fronting and postponing among its clauses: «يا ...» was chosen rather than the rest of its sisters because it is more frequent in use, and because it indicates the distance of the one addressed, which the situation of displaying greatness and showing the dignity of might and omnipotence calls for. As for looking at the order of the clauses: the vocative was put before the command, so it was said: «يا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي ...» «وَيا سَماءُ أَقْلِعِي ...»
rather than saying: "Swallow, O earth, and desist, O sky", following what is required – in the case of one who is truly commanded – of putting the alerting first, so that the command coming after it may settle firmly in the soul of the one addressed, intending thereby the meaning of tarshīḥ for the implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in the earth and the sky. Then He put the command to the earth before the command to the sky, because it is the origin, given that the deluge began from it, as its oven gushed forth first.
All this is examining the āya from the two sides of rhetoric. Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ mentioned that it contains twenty kinds of badīʿ (embellishment), although it is seventeen words, namely: complete correspondence (munāsaba tāmma) in «ابلعي ...» and «اقلعي ...»; the istiʿāra in them; the ṭibāq (antithesis) between the earth and the sky; the majāz in «يا سَماءُ ...», for the literal is "O rain of the sky"; ishāra (allusion) in «وَغِيضَ الْماءُ ...», for many meanings are expressed by it, because the water does not abate until the rain of the sky desists and the earth swallows what comes out of it, so what is on the face of the earth decreases; irdāf (expressing by a consequent) in «وَاسْتَوَتْ ...»; tamthīl (representation) in «وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ ...»; taʿlīl (causation), for the abating of the water is the cause of the settling; ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm (sound division), for it covers the divisions of the water in the state of its decrease; iḥtirās (precaution) in the imprecation, lest it be imagined that the drowning, because of its generality, included those who did not deserve destruction, for His justice, the Exalted, prevents Him from invoking against one who does not deserve it; ḥusn al-nasaq (fine sequence); iʾtilāf al-lafẓ maʿa al-maʿnā (harmony of wording with meaning); ījāz (concision), for He, glory be to Him, told the story comprehensively in the briefest expression; tashīm (foreshadowing), because the beginning of the āya indicates its end; tahdhīb (refinement), because its individual words are described with attributes of beauty; ḥusn al-bayān (clarity of exposition), in that the listener does not hesitate in understanding the meaning of the speech and nothing of it is obscure to him; tamkīn (settledness), because the fāṣila (verse-ending) is settled in its place, at rest in its position; and insijām (flow). Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī added iʿtirāḍ (parenthesis).
[Translator's note: the list as given in the source names fewer than twenty kinds; it is translated as written.]

* Benefits:
1- Rhetorical inimitability in the Qurʾān:
This āya comprises arts of rhetoric exceeding twenty-five arts, which the scholars of rhetoric have mentioned in detail and there is no room to set them out; one can only fall prostrate before the greatness of Allah, mighty and majestic, and bow before His inimitable expression, acknowledging that falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it, a revelation from One Wise, Praiseworthy. It is related that a great scholar tried to criticize the Noble Qurʾān by discovering a simple flaw in it, and the attempt went on for months; he had a group who kept coming to him and asking him what he had done. But in the end he broke the pen and the inkwell and said: This is the speech of Allah; it is not to be disputed. Then he passed by a mosque and heard a boy reciting this āya, and he said: It is not for a human being to say speech like this.
2- Imām al-Nasafī's comment on this āya:
And from the angle of eloquence of meaning: it is, as you see, a subtle arrangement of the meanings, and a conveying of them summarized and made clear; no complexity besets the mind in seeking what is intended, and no twisting makes the road to the seeker doubtful. And from the angle of eloquence of wording: its words, as you see, are Arabic and in use, free from dissonance, far from ugliness, sweet on the tongue-tips, smooth on the tongue-edges; each of them is like water in smoothness, like honey in sweetness, and like the breeze in gentleness. Hence the obstinate opponents agreed that human capacity falls short of producing the like of this āya. How excellent is the status of the Revelation! A scholar does not contemplate one of its āyas without perceiving subtleties beyond counting; and do not think the āya is restricted to what has been mentioned, for perhaps what has been left out is more than what has been written.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (نادى نوح ربّه) like نادى نوح ابنه [Note: In āya (42) of this sūra.], (الفاء) conjunction (قال) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he" (ربّ) the one addressed, a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb); the vocative particle has been dropped from it, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ dropped for lightness.. and (الياء), dropped, is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ابني) the noun of inna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, [attached to] the khabar (predicate) of inna [Translator's note: the source reads "جارّ ومجرور بخبر إنّ", apparently missing the word متعلّق], and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (إنّ وعدك) like إنّ ابني, the fatḥa being overt (الحقّ) the khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) (الواو) conjunction (أنت) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (أحكم) khabar, nominative (الحاكمين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «نادى نوح ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نادى, and it is an explicative or detailing conjunction.
The clause «ربّ ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) [Note: Or it is parenthetical with no grammatical position, and the clause after it is the object of the saying.].
The clause «إنّ ابني من أهلي» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ وعدك الحقّ» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause that is the reply to the vocative.
The clause «أنت أحكم الحاكمين» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause that is the reply to the vocative.

* Benefits:
Was Canaan (Kanʿān), the drowned one, the son of Nūḥ? Most exegetes hold that he was Nūḥ's son from his own loins.
This is the correct view, and whatever is other than it is false. The majority have transmitted what is authentic from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The wife of a prophet never committed fornication (mā baghat, i.e. mā zanat). And He, the Exalted, stated explicitly in His saying وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ, just as his father called him in his saying (يا بني اركب معنا). The exegetes said: If the wife of a prophet disbelieves, this does not disgrace him or touch his honour; but fornication is a disgrace and may never occur from the wife of a prophet, as has come from Ibn ʿAbbās. What appears to me – and Allah knows best – is that His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed he is not of your family" means that by his choosing disbelief the moral kinship between him and his father was cut off, because faith is the fundamental bond and the true kinship.

safi-cedvel:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negating; (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (دابّة) genitive (majrūr) in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, mubtadaʾ (subject); (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of «دابّة»; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate); (رزق) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), in the position of the genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (مستقرّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (ها) like the first; (الواو) conjunction; (مستودعها) like «مستقرّها» and conjoined to it; (كلّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: What permitted beginning with an indefinite noun is that it denotes generality, and that it is on the assumption of an implied muḍāf, i.e.: every thing in life.. or everything mentioned at the beginning of the verse.]; (في كتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (مبين) a naʿt of «كتاب», genitive.
The clause «ما من دابّة ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «على الله رزقها» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ «دابّة».
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the preceding khabar clause.
The clause «كلّ في كتاب ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive and causal (taʿlīliyya).
(الواو) conjunction; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (خلق) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he", and it is the resumptive pronoun; (السموات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the kasra; (الأرض) conjoined to «السموات» by the wāw, accusative; (في ستة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلق); (أيّام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) parenthetical; (كان) a defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) —; (عرش) the noun of kāna, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, in the position of the genitive; (على الماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of kāna; (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (يبلو) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبلوكم..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (خلق); (أيّ) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (أحسن) khabar, nominative; (عملا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) paving the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive (majzūm); (قلت) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator — and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna; (مبعوثون) the khabar of inna, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the wāw; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (مبعوثون); (الموت) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يقولنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, fāʿil; (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is fāʿil; (إن) a negating particle; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (سحر) khabar, nominative; (مبين) a naʿt of «سحر», nominative.
The clause «هو الذي ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause «ما من دابة..».
The clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun «الذي».
The clause «كان عرشه على الماء» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
The clause «يبلوكم ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أيّكم أحسن ...» is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb of testing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from operating by the interrogative [Note: This is according to the view of al-Zamakhsharī, and Abū Ḥayyān followed him, because testing contains the sense of knowing; but Ibn Hishām rejected this analysis, so the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «قلت ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «إنّكم مبعوثون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يقولنّ الذين كفروا» has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath..
And the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إن هذا إلّا سحر» is in the position of the accusative as the second object of saying.
(الواو) conjunction; (لئن أخّرنا) like «لئن قلت»; (عن) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أخّرنا); (العذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (إلى أمّة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخّرنا); (معدودة) a naʿt of «أمّة», genitive; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يقولنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, which has been deleted because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is a pronoun in the position of the nominative, fāʿil, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (يحبس) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he". (ألا) a particle of alerting; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (مصروفا); (يأتي) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "it", i.e., the punishment, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (ليس) a defective, inflexible (jāmid) past verb — an abrogator — and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (مصروفا) the khabar of laysa, accusative; (عنهم) like the first, attached to (مصروفا); (الواو) conjunction; (حاق) a past verb; (بهم) like «عنهم», attached to (حاق); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, fāʿil; (كانوا) a defective past verb — an abrogator — indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, the noun of kāna; (به) like «عنهم», attached to (يستهزئون), which is an imperfect verb, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil.
The clause «إن أخرنا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إن قلت».
The clause «يقولنّ ...» has no grammatical position; the response to the oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «ما يحبسه» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying.
The clause «يحبسه» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of «ما».
The clause «يأتيهم» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ليس مصروفا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «حاق بهم ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «ليس مصروفا».
The clause «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يستهزئون» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of «كانوا».
(الواو) conjunction; (لئن أذقنا) like «لئن قلت»; (الإنسان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an [omitted] ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رحمة» — a naʿt placed before the noun it qualifies —; (رحمة) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (نزعنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil, and the verb is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to (أذقنا), and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (منه) like «منّا», attached to (نزعنا); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis [Note: This lām is obligatory here because the clause is the response to the oath, so the lām has the status of the lām of the oath.]. (يئوس) the khabar of inna, nominative [Translator's note: the source repeats «مرفوع».]; (كفور) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إن أذقنا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إن قلت»..
The clause «نزعناها ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إن أذقنا».
The clause «إنّه ليؤوس ...» has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath..
And the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
(الواو) conjunction; (لئن أذقنا) like «لئن قلت», and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (نعماء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and it is prevented from taking tanwīn because it ends in the extended alif of the feminine; (بعد) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أذقناه); (ضرّاء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is like «نعماء»; (مسّ) a past verb, and (التاء) is the tāʾ of the feminine, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya"; (ليقولنّ) like the first, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (ذهب) like «خلق»; (السيّئات) fāʿil, nominative; (عنّي) like «عنهم», and in it is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) before the yāʾ of the speaker, attached to (ذهب); (إنّه لفرح فخور) like «إنّه ليؤوس كفور».
The clause «إن أذقناه ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إن قلت».
The clause «مسّته ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of «ضرّاء».
The clause «يقولنّ» has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «ذهب السيّئات» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying.
The clause «إنّه لفرح ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the genitive pronoun, so it is a ḥāl corroborating the content of the clause before it [Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
(إلّا) a particle of exception [Note: It may mean «لكن» ("but"), and what follows it is a nominal clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar.]; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the excepted in a connected exception [Note: from «الإنسان» mentioned earlier in the previous verse, which denotes the genus.. And the exception may be disconnected if «الإنسان» is a specific man.]; (صبروا) like «كفروا», and like it is (عملوا); (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the kasra; (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (مغفرة) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أجر) conjoined to «مغفرة» by the wāw, nominative; (كبير) a naʿt of «أجر», nominative.
The clause «صبروا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك لهم مغفرة ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لهم مغفرة ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).

* Morphology:
(مصروفا): passive participle of the triliteral صرف; its pattern is مفعول.
(حاق): it contains a weakening by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is «حيق», its imperfect «يحيق»; the yāʾ came voweled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif.. See verse (10) of Sūrat al-Anʿām.
(يئوس): intensive form of the active participle from «يئس ييئس», of the فرح class; its pattern is فعول.. It may be an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha).
(كفور): intensive form of the active participle from «كفر يكفر», of the نصر class; its pattern is فعول..

* Morphology:
(نوفّ): it contains a weakening by deletion on account of the jussive; its original form is «نوفّي», and it may be an assimilated adjective [Translator's note: so in the source; this word belongs to verse 15 and the final remark appears misplaced.].
(نعماء): a noun meaning «النعمى» (blessing), from «نعم ينعم» of the first, third and fourth classes; its pattern is فعلاء, and the hamza is added for the feminine.

* Rhetoric:
1- The saying of the Exalted: «إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ», i.e., like it in deception and falsehood; the construction is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh), and what is meant is denial of the resurrection by way of allusive metonymy (kināya īmāʾiyya).
2- Implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): in the saying of the Exalted «وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً», i.e., We gave him a blessing of health, security and wealth. Tasting (al-idhāqa) originally is taking something with the mouth to perceive food; then it was borrowed for pleasure, likening it to what is tasted and then quickly disappears, as flavours disappear.
3- Antithesis (ṭibāq): between «النعماء» and «الضراء».

* Benefits:
- Suspending the verb from operating (taʿlīq):
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted: لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا. In this verse we say that the verb (يبلوكم) is suspended from putting the mafʿūl bihi in the accusative, because the mafʿūl bihi comes as a nominal clause headed by an interrogative. In the i'rab we say: «أيكم» is a mubtadaʾ, nominative, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the mīm is for the plural; «أحسن» is khabar, nominative; and the clause «أيكم أحسن» is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb «يبلوكم».
It is useful in this context to mention a brief account of what relates to this important topic:
1- A verb that is transitive to one object may be suspended from operating, and that is when the clause is headed by an interrogative, as in the saying of the Exalted: فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّها أَزْكى طَعاماً and the saying of the Exalted: يَسْئَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ 2- And a verb that is transitive to two objects may be suspended from operating if the clause is headed by an interrogative, and we parse it as a clause standing in place of the two objects, as in the saying of the Exalted: وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنا أَشَدُّ عَذاباً لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصى

safi-cedvel:88-89.t:
* I'rab:
(قال يا قوم ... رزقا حسنا) the i'rab of its parallel has passed [Note: In verse (28) of this sura.], and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "shall I go against His command?" (هل أخالف أمره) [Note: Or "shall I betray His revelation?".. or "shall I follow error?", or "shall I defraud people of their things?".. etc.]; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a particle of negation; (أريد) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "I" (أنا); (أن أخالفكم) like أن نترك [Note: In verse (87) of this sura.], and (كم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the interpreted maṣdar (أن أخالفكم) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being the negated أريد.
(إلى) a preposition; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخالف) [Note: (ما) may be an indefinite noun described by a following clause, in the position of genitive.. and the clause after it is its naʿt (adjective), in the position of genitive.]; (أنهاكم) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is "I".. and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (عن) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنهاكم); (إن) a particle of negation; (أريد) like the first; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الإصلاح) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (ما) a maṣdar-forming temporal particle; (استطعت) past verb and its fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما استطعت..) is in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (أريد), i.e. "I want reform for as long as I am able".
(الواو) conjunction; (ما) a particle of negation; (توفيقي) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied on what precedes the yāʾ, and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلّا) like the first; (بالله) preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (عليه) like عنه, attached to (توكّلت), which is parsed like استطعت; (الواو) conjunction; (إليه) like عنه, attached to (أنيب), which is parsed like أريد.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its response ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أرأيتم ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «إن كنت ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech.
The clause «رزقني ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the parenthetical clause.
The clause «ما أريد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «أخالفكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أنهاكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إن أريد ...» has no grammatical position: justificatory (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «استطعت» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «ما توفيقي إلّا بالله» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «عليه توكّلت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive within the scope of the speech.
The clause «إليه أنيب» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause توكّلت.
(الواو) conjunction; (يا قوم) like the first; (لا) the prohibitive lā, making jussive; (يجرمنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (كم) is a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (شقاقي) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi [Note: This pronoun is, in meaning, the object of the maṣdar, i.e. "your hostility to me".]; (أن يصيبكم) like أن أخالفكم [Note: In verse (88) of this sura.]; (مثل) fāʿil, nominative [Note: It is originally the adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. "a punishment like what befell ...".]; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (أصاب) past verb, and the fāʿil is "he/it" (هو), which is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (قوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (نوح) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (أو) a conjunction in both places; (قوم هود — قوم صالح) like قوم نوح, both conjoined to it; (الواو) resumptive; (ما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد) like ما هي من الظالمين ببعيد [Note: In verse (83) of this sura.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يصيبكم) is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being يجرمنّكم.
The clause «يا قوم» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the first clause يا قوم.
The clause «لا يجرمنكم شقاقي» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «يصيبكم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أصاب ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «ما قوم.. ببعيد» has no grammatical position: resumptive or parenthetical.

* Morphology:
(استطعت): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion in keeping with being built on the sukūn; its origin is استطاعت, and when the verb was built on the sukūn because of its being attached to the nominative pronoun, the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; its pattern is استفلت.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb, for hope (tarajjī) [Note: It is said to be for affirmation (taqrīr).. and it is said to be for interrogation.. and it is said to be for making remote (tabʿīd), because hope, which entails expectation, does not befit the station of prophethood.] — an abrogator (nāsikh) —; (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of laʿalla; (تارك) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (بعض) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «تارك», accusative (manṣūb); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (يوحى) a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and it is the resumptive pronoun; (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يوحى); (الواو) conjunction; (ضائق) conjoined to «تارك», nominative [Note: or it is a fronted khabar and (صدرك) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).. and the clause is conjoined to «تارك».]; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to «ضائق»; (صدر) fāʿil (agent) of the active participle «ضائق», nominative, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative; (يقولوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil; (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning «هلّا»; (أنزل) a passive past verb; (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أنزل); (كنز) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative; (أو) a conjunction; (جاء) a past verb; (مع) an adverb (ẓarf), accusative, attached to (جاء) [Note: or attached to an [omitted] ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ملك».], and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ملك) fāʿil, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقولوا) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e., "for fear that they say" [Note: It may be genitive by an implied lām of causation, negated, i.e., «لئلّا يقولوا» ("lest they say") ...]; (إنّما) the restraining mā with what it restrains (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (أنت) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (نذير) khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «وكيل»; (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (وكيل) khabar, nominative.
The clause «لعلّك تارك ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
