(يصدّون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the واو is the fāʿil (عن سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يصدّون), (الله) the Word of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) conjunction (يبغون) like يصدّون, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (عوجا) a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (الواو) conjunction (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (بالآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كافرون), the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; the second (هم) is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of the first.
The clause «يصدّون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يبغونها ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «هم ... كافرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(الأشهاد): plural of شاهد on the pattern فاعل, or of شهيد on the pattern فعيل; a derived adjective from شهد يشهد, of the class فرح.
(يبغون): it contains iʿlāl by vowel-dropping (taskīn) and iʿlāl by deletion (ḥadhf). Its original form is يبغيون with a ḍamma on the second yāʾ; the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent — this is iʿlāl by taskīn — and its vowel was transferred to the غ before it; then the yāʾ was deleted because it met, quiescent, the واو of the plural — iʿlāl by deletion. Its pattern is يفعون.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(أولئك) mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: See āya (18) of this sūra.], (لم) a particle of negation and jussive (يكونوا) a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the واو is the noun of kāna (معجزين) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; معجزين is the khabar of يكونوا, while the clause «لم يكونوا…» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, as stated below.] (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) معجزين (الواو) conjunction (ما) negating (كان) a defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted khabar of kāna (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) from أولياء (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition (أولياء) genitive in form, nominative in position, the postponed noun of kāna; the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, since it is a diptote, being a noun ending in the extended feminine alif on the pattern أفعلاء (يضاعف) imperfect verb, passive, nominative (لهم) like the first, attached to (يضاعف), (العذاب) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (ما) like the first one [Note: al-ʿUkbarī allowed taking it as a temporal maṣdariyya, i.e. for the duration of their being able to hear..], (كانوا) a defective past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the واو is the noun of kāna (يستطيعون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the واو is the fāʿil (agent) (السمع) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (الواو) conjunction (ما كانوا يبصرون) like ما كانوا يستطيعون.
The clause «أولئك لم يكونوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لم يكونوا معجزين ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.
The clause «ما كان لهم ... أولياء» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.
The clause «يضاعف لهم العذاب» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما كانوا يستطيعون ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يستطيعون السمع» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of (the first) كانوا.
The clause «ما كانوا يبصرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the causal clause.
The clause «يبصرون» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of (the second) كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
Dependent explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «ما كانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ», i.e. they found it extremely heavy and loathsome to hear the truth which the Messenger ﷺ brought, to the utmost degree, as though they were unable to do so. It is like someone's saying: the lover cannot bear to hear the words of the one who reproaches him.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(أولئك الذين) mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) — their i'rab has already been given [Note: In āya (16) of this sūra.] —, (خسروا) like كذبوا [Note: In āya (18) of this sūra.], (أنفس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (ضلّ) past verb (عن) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ضلّ) by its implying the meaning of غاب ("was absent") (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the returning pronoun is omitted (كانوا يفترون) like كانوا يستطيعون [Note: In the previous āya (20).].
[Translator's note: so in the source; (ما) here is ordinarily the fāʿil (agent) of ضلّ, which is intransitive.]
The clause «أولئك الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خسروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ضلّ.. ما كانوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «كانوا يفترون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يفترون» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of كانوا.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) the lā of generic negation (جرم) the noun of lā, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative [Note: We have preferred the i'rab of the majority — contrary to Sībawayh — because it is easier and needs no reinterpretation.
The āya may also be parsed as follows: لا: negating. جرم: past verb meaning وجب ("became binding"), حقّ or ثبت ("was established").. and the interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم.. الأخسرون) is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent), i.e. their loss in the Hereafter is established.
The two words (لا جرم) may also be combined into a single word meaning حقّا ("truly"), in which case it is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).. and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil of the maṣdar حقا, i.e. truly is their loss. There are other analyses which we have passed over because they are far-fetched.], (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna (في الآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (الأخسرون), (هم) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is الأخسرون.. and the nominal clause is the khabar of anna.], (الأخسرون) khabar of anna, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the واو.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنهم.. الأخسرون) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being في or من, i.e. في أنهم.. or من أنّهم; attached to the khabar of lā.
The clause «لا جرم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(جرم): it may be a noun meaning محالة ("no escape"), or meaning حدّ ("limit"), منع ("prevention") or قطع ("cutting").. and it may be a verb meaning كسب ("earned"), or meaning حقّ and ثبت ("was established").. Its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas [Note: Thus it appeared in the manuscript. al-Munjid says: جرم النخل: he picked the fruit of the palm; جرم الشيء: he completed it; اجترم لأهله: he earned for his family.]

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna (آمنوا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (الواو) conjunction (عملوا) like آمنوا (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra (الواو) conjunction (أخبتوا) like آمنوا (إلى ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخبتوا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (أولئك) mubtadaʾ (subject), as before [Note: In āya (16) of this sūra.], (أصحاب) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) (الجنة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (في) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (خالدون), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the واو.
The clause «إنّ الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أخبتوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك أصحاب ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna.
The clause «هم فيها خالدون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from أصحاب [Note: Or in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).].

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(مثل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) (الفريقين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (كالأعمى) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. كمثل الأعمى; the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif (الأصمّ) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الأعمى by the واو, genitive, and likewise (البصير), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. مثل البصير, genitive (السميع) conjoined to البصير by the واو, genitive (هل) an interrogative particle of disapproval (inkār) [Note: Or of negation, i.e. they are not equal in likeness.] (يستويان) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn..
and (الألف) an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent) (مثلا) tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb) (الهمزة) for the interrogative of disapproval (الفاء) conjunction (لا) negating (تذكّرون) imperfect verb, nominative, from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted.. and the واو is the fāʿil.
The clause «مثل الفريقين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هل يستويان ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تذكّرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. أجهلتم فلا تذكّرون.

* Morphology:
(الأصمّ): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) on the pattern أفعل, from صمّ يصمّ, of the class فتح; its feminine is صمّاء and its plural is صمّ and صمان, with a ḍamma on the ṣād in both. (تذكّرون): one of the two tāʾs was deleted in it for lightness; its original form is تتذكّرون.

* Rhetoric:
Simile (tashbīh): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «مَثَلُ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ كَالْأَعْمى وَالْأَصَمِّ وَالْبَصِيرِ وَالسَّمِيعِ», i.e. like the state of one who combines blindness and deafness, and of one who combines sight and hearing. So there are two similes: the first likens the state of the disbelievers, described as feigning blindness and deafness toward the signs of Allah, to the state of one created blind and deaf, whom neither words nor gestures benefit; the second likens the state of those who believed and did righteous deeds, and so benefited from their hearing and sight, to the state of one who sees and hears, who seeks the shade of lights in the darkness and seeks the spoils of warning and indication, attaining his goal. [Translator's note: so in the source, «يستفيء» twice; the sense is "draws benefit from".]
It is also possible that there are four similes, by considering the state of each of the two groups — the disbelieving group and the believing group — to be likened to the state of two. That is: the likeness of the disbelieving group is like the blind, and its likeness is also like the deaf; and the likeness of the believing group is like the seeing, and its likeness is also like the hearing. In all its possibilities, the āya bears a general resemblance to the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
كأن قلوب الطير رطبا ويابسا ... لدى وكرها العناب والحشف البالي
(As though the hearts of birds, fresh and dry, by her nest were jujube berries and old withered dates.)
In the verse, the fresh hearts of the birds are likened to jujubes, and the dry hearts of the birds to old withered dates.
But the āya goes further by likening two to four, as is clear: it likens each of the disbeliever and the believer with two similes.

safi-cedvel:57-57.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction (إن) a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive (تولّوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), one of its two tāʾs having been dropped, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (الفاء) causal [Note: Or it binds the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause after it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, even though it carries the sense of causation.] (قد) particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (أبلغت) past verb and its agent, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (أرسلت) past verb, passive.. and (التاء) a pronoun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلت) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the deputy agent, i.e. "I was sent charged with conveying it to you", and there is an omitted muḍāf in the expression.], (إلى) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أرسلت). (الواو) resumptive (يستخلف) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) (ربّي) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ.. and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (قوما) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) (غيركم) naʿt (adjective) of (قوما), accusative.. and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (لا) negative (تضرّون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the agent, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun) because it is of the kind of the description, i.e. "any harm at all" (إنّ ربّي على كلّ) like the preceding one [Note: In the previous āya (56).], and the prepositional phrase is attached to حفيظ (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (حفيظ) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative.
The clause «إن تولّوا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «قد أبلغتكم ...» has no grammatical position; a causal explanation of the implied apodosis, i.e. "if you turn away, I do not care, because I have conveyed to you".
The clause «أرسلت به ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يستخلف ربّي ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «لا تضرّونه شيئا» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّ ربّي.... حفيظ» has no grammatical position; causal.

* Benefits:
- Omission of the apodosis clause:
1- The apodosis must be omitted if something indicating it precedes, e.g. هو ظالم إن فعل, the implied form being إن فعل فهو ظالم.
2- The apodosis may be omitted in other cases, as in His saying, the Exalted, فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي الْأَرْضِ, i.e. "then do so". And وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ, i.e. "they would not have believed in it", as indicated by وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِالرَّحْمنِ.
3- The verified and correct view is that among the cases in which the apodosis is omitted is His saying, the Exalted, مَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا لِقاءَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ لَآتٍ, because the apodosis is caused by the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), whereas Allah's term is coming whether the hope exists or not; rather, the underlying form is that the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "let him hasten to act, for Allah's term is coming". Similar to it is His saying, the Exalted, وَإِنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ, i.e. "then be patient", فَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ. And His saying, the Exalted, إِنْ يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ, i.e. "then be patient", فَقَدْ مَسَّ الْقَوْمَ قَرْحٌ مِثْلُهُ. Of the same kind is what occurs in the āya under discussion: the apodosis of the condition (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا) has been omitted, i.e. the apodosis is "then there is no blame on me", (فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ).

safi-cedvel:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نجينا), (جاء) past verb (أمر) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (نجّينا) past verb and its agent (هودا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (الواو) conjunction (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, conjoined to (هودا), (آمنوا) past verb and its agent (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (آمنوا), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (برحمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نجينا), and the bāʾ is causal (من) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة (الواو) the resumptive wāw (نجّينا) like the first, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (من عذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نجّيناهم), (غليظ) naʿt of عذاب, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «جاء أمرنا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نجّينا ...» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «نجّيناهم ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: The first deliverance is in this world and the second in the Hereafter, so it is not restricted by the condition, and therefore it was not conjoined to the first.].

safi-cedvel:59-60.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (تلك) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In āya (49) of this sūra.], (عاد) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) (جحدوا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جحدوا), (ربّهم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).. and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (عصوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (رسل) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (اتّبعوا) like جحدوا (أمر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (كلّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (جبّار) like كلّ (عنيد) naʿt (adjective) of جبّار, genitive.
The clause «تلك عاد ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «جحدوا ...» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) تلك [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
The clause «عصوا ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause جحدوا.
The clause «اتّبعوا» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause جحدوا.
(الواو) conjunction (أتبعوا) past verb, passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma..
and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (في) a preposition (ها) particle of alerting (ذه) demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of genitive, attached to (أتبعوا), (الدنيا) badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, following it in the genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif (لعنة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) conjunction (يوم) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أتبعوا), so it is conjoined to the semi-clause (في هذه), (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (ألا) particle of alerting (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — (عادا) the noun of inna, accusative (كفروا) like جحدوا (ربّهم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, by كفروا being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of جحدوا, just as جحدوا was made to include the meaning of كفروا in the previous āya.. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (ألا) like the first (بعدا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb (لعاد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (بعدا) [Note: See the i'rab of بعدا للقوم الظالمين (āya 44 of this sūra).], (قوم) badal of عاد, genitive (هود) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «أتبعوا ...» is conjoined to the clause جحدوا and takes its i'rab.
The clause «إنّ عادا كفروا ...» has no grammatical position; a causal explanation of what preceded.
The clause «كفروا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «(أبعدوا) بعدا» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(عنيد), a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the verb عند يعند, of the pattern-class of naṣara, ḍaraba, fariḥa and karuma; its pattern is فعيل; [it means] one who opposes the truth while knowing it.
(هود), it is declined as a triptote because it is not foreign; it is Arabic. Ibn Hishām said in al-Shudhūr [Note: al-Shudhūr p. (555).]: Among the prophets there is none who is an Arab except Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Shuʿayb and Muḥammad, Allah's blessings and peace be upon them. Its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma followed by sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Metaphorical attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَتِلْكَ عادٌ» there is reference to the distant perceptible and metaphorical attribution. Or it is a figure of omission (majāz al-ḥadhf), i.e. "those are the graves of ʿĀd".

safi-cedvel:61-61.t:
* I'rab:
(وإلى ثمود.. إله غيره) the i'rab of its parallel has already been given [Note: In āya (50) of this sūra.], (هو) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (أنشأ) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he" (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (من الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنشأكم), (الواو) conjunction (استعمركم) like أنشأكم (في) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (استعمركم), (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (استغفروا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (ثمّ) a conjunction (توبوا) like استغفروا (إلى) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (توبوا), (إنّ ربّي قريب مجيب) like إنّ ربّي لغفور رحيم [Note: In āya (41) of this sūra.].
The clause «(أرسلنا) إلى ثمود ...» is conjoined to the clause (أرسلنا) إلى عاد [Note: In āya (50) of this sūra.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The vocative clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «ما لكم من إله غيره» has no grammatical position; causal — or an explanatory resumption.
The clause «هو أنشأكم ...» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «أنشأكم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هو.
The clause «استعمركم ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أنشأكم.
The clause «استغفروه» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you sin, then ask His forgiveness".
The clause «توبوا إليه» is conjoined to the clause استغفروه.
The clause «إنّ ربّي قريب» has no grammatical position; causal.

* Morphology:
(ثمود), a proper name of the father of the tribe; it [the tribe] was named after him because of his fame. It is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) because of being a proper name and foreign. The tribe of Thamūd is the one that lived in al-Ḥijr, which is a place between al-Shām and Medina.
(صالح), a proper name, and it is an Arabic word because it is on the pattern فاعل, and this pattern is more associated with nouns than with verbs; for that reason it is declined as a triptote.
(مجيب), active participle of the quadriliteral أجاب, so it is on the pattern مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by quiescence and iʿlāl by conversion.. the weak letter was made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the letter before it, the jīm. The original of مجيب is مجوب — with sukūn on the jīm and kasra on the wāw — because the wāw appears in the maṣdar (verbal noun) جواب; when it was made quiescent and the letter before it had kasra, it was converted into yāʾ, giving مجيب.

safi-cedvel:62-62.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (يا) vocative particle (صالح) the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper name, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative (قد) particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (كنت) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun (في) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مرجوا), which is the khabar (predicate) of the defective verb, accusative (manṣūb) (قبل) adverb of time, accusative, attached to the khabar, and (ها) particle of alerting (ذا) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الهمزة) for interrogation expressing astonishment (تنهى) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is "you", and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative (نعبد) imperfect verb, accusative, and the agent is "we" (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (يعبد) like نعبد (آباء) fāʿil, nominative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن نعبد..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being عن, attached to (تنهانا) (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial) (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) (في شك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of inna (من) a preposition (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to شكّ (تدعو) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the wāw, and the agent is "you", and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (مريب) naʿt (adjective) of شكّ, genitive (majrūr) like it.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The vocative clause «يا صالح ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قد كنت ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «أتنهانا ...» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «نعبد ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يعبد آباؤنا» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّنا لفي شكّ..» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the object in (تنهانا).
The clause «تدعونا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(مرجوّا), passive participle of رجا يرجو; its pattern is مفعول. The wāw of مفعول has been assimilated (idghām) into the final radical of the word. Its meaning is that we placed our hope in you that you would be a chief for us or a counsellor in affairs.
(تنهى), it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion: the original of the alif is yāʾ, because the maṣdar is نهي; when the yāʾ came voweled after a fatḥa it was converted into alif.
(مريب), active participle of the quadriliteral أراب, i.e. "he cast him into doubt", or of the intransitive أراب, i.e. "he became a possessor of doubt"; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. It contains iʿlāl by quiescence: its original is مريب with sukūn on the rāʾ and kasra on the yāʾ; the kasra was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the rāʾ before it, so it became (مريب).

safi-cedvel:25-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (أرسلنا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent) (نوحا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (إلى قوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (نذير), which is the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) (مبين) naʿt (adjective) of نذير, nominative.
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to an implied oath.. and the oath clause together with its answer has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّي لكم نذير ...» is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech) of an implied verb of saying.. and the implied saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (نوحا).
(أن) an explicative particle [Note: The particle is preceded by a verb which has the meaning of saying without its letters, namely his saying إنّي لكم نذير مبين, i.e. أنذركم ("I warn you"), i.e. I say to you as a warner. There are other permissible explanations, as in āya (2) of this sūra (Part 11).], (لا) the prohibitive, governing the jussive (تعبدوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the واو is the fāʿil (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) (الله) the Word of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative (إنّي) like the first (أخاف) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنا (عليكم) like لكم, attached to (أخاف) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl from عذاب.], (عذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (أليم) naʿt of يوم, genitive [Note: Painfulness describes the punishment, not the day, so this is figurative attribution (isnād majāzī).].
The clause «لا تعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «إنّي أخاف ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أخاف ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna.
(الفاء) conjunction (قال) past verb (الملأ) fāʿil, nominative (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as naʿt of الملأ, (كفروا) past verb and its fāʿil (من قوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of كفروا, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (ما) negating (نرى) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being نحن, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (إلّا) a particle of restriction (بشرا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: Or a ḥāl, if the seeing is visual.], (مثل) naʿt of (بشرا), accusative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi [Note: Or a second ḥāl from the pronoun of address.], (الواو) conjunction (ما نراك) like the first (اتّبع) past verb, and (الكاف) mafʿūl bihi (إلّا) like the first (الذين) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil [Note: (إلّا) may be a particle of exception, and الذين a badal (substitute) from the implied fāʿil, i.e. ما نراك اتّبعك إنسان إلّا الذين.. and the relative noun may be accusative as the excepted.], (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (أراذل) khabar, nominative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (بادي) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (اتّبع) [Note: Or to the verb نراك. In Lisān al-ʿArab it says: «وانتصاب من همز ومن لم يهمز- أي بادئ أو بادي- بالاتباع على مذهب المصدر أي اتّبعوك اتّباعا ظاهرا أو اتّباعا مبتدأ. وإذا كانت بادي الرأي بمعنى ظاهر الرأي يجوز إعرابها منصوبة على نزع الخافض أي: في بادي الرأي» ("Those who read it with a hamza and those who read it without — i.e. بادئ or بادي — make it accusative by اتّبع in the manner of a maṣdar, i.e. they followed you with an apparent following, or with a first following. And if بادي الرأي means 'the apparent view', it may be parsed as accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. في بادي الرأي").], (الرأي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) conjunction (ما نرى) like the first (لكم) its i'rab has already been given; attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of (نرى), (على) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl from فضل — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies — (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition (فضل) genitive in form, accusative in position, first mafʿūl bihi (بل) a particle of digression (iḍrāb) (نظنّكم) like نراك, with the ḍamma overt (كاذبين) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال الملأ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the implied oath clause.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ما نراك (the first)» is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «ما نراك (the second)» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «اتّبعك إلّا الذين ...» is in the position of the accusative as second mafʿūl bihi of the second (نراك) [Note: If رأى is visual, the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied.].
The clause «هم أراذلنا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ما نرى....» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «نظنّكم كاذبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أراذل): plural of أرذل — with a ḍamma on the ذال — which is the plural of رذل — with it quiescent; a derived adjective which has come to be used predominantly as a noun, so that the qualified noun is hardly ever mentioned with it, like الأبطح and الأبرق. It is also said that (أراذل) is the plural of أرذل on the pattern أكبر, so it is not a plural of a plural; the pattern of أراذل is أفاعل.
(بادي): either from the verb بدأ, its pattern being فاعل, i.e. بادئ, then the hamza was lightened and changed into a yāʾ because of the kasra before it.. or it is from the verb بدا يبدو, its pattern being فاعل, and it contains iʿlāl by changing the واو into a yāʾ because it is quiescent and preceded by a kasra, its original form being بادو.. Under both views it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like العافية and العاقبة.
(الرأي): it is seeing with the mind, just as ruʾya is seeing with the eye.. see āya (13) of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.

* Rhetoric:
Allusion (taʿrīḍ): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «فَقالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ ما نَراكَ إِلَّا بَشَراً مِثْلَنا وَما نَراكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ هُمْ أَراذِلُنا بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ». Their aim here is to allude that they are more entitled to prophethood than he, and that if Allah had wished to place it in anyone He would have placed it in them. These people claimed that they were refuting Nūḥ from two angles: first, that his followers are the lowest of people, neither an example nor a model; second, that even so they did not deliberate in following him, nor reflect deeply on the soundness of what he brought, but rushed to it impulsively, without thought or deliberation.

* Benefits:
- (أن) and its possible i'rab analyses:
In this āya comes the saying of Allah the Exalted أَنْ لا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ. (أن) in this āya has three analyses, which we shall set out, showing what follows from each for the i'rab of what comes after it:
1- أن: an explicative particle; لا is the prohibitive, governing the jussive, and the verb after it is jussive.
2- أن: lightened from the heavy form (anna); its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), لا is the prohibitive, governing the jussive, and the verb after it is jussive. The implied form is أنه لا تعبدوا إلا الله.
3- أن: a particle governing the subjunctive; لا is negating without any governing effect, and the verb تعبدوا is subjunctive (manṣūb) by أن.

safi-cedvel:28-31.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he" (يا) a vocative particle (قوم) the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the omitted yāʾ, and (الياء), omitted for lightness, is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الهمزة) for interrogation (رأيتم) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil, in the sense of أخبروني ("tell me"); the object of رأيتم is omitted, indicated by the word البيّنة after the condition, i.e. أرأيتم البيّنة (إن) a conditional particle governing the jussive (كنت) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (التاء) is the noun of kāna (على بيّنة) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of كنت (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt (adjective) of بيّنة, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (آتى) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif, and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "he" (رحمة) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt of رحمة, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) conjunction (عمّيت) past verb, passive.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هي — i.e. the clear proof — (على) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عمّيت), (الهمزة) for interrogation (نلزم) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and (الواو) is redundant (zāʾida), being the lengthening (ishbāʿ) of the vowel of the mīm, and (ها) a pronoun, second mafʿūl bihi; and the fāʿil is نحن, for majesty (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (اللام) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (كارهون), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the واو.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «أرأيتم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «كنت على بيّنة ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, occurring between the verb and its object.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «آتاني رحمة ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, between the clause كنت على بيّنة and the clause عمّيت conjoined to it [Note: The pronoun in عمّيت may refer back to رحمة.. in which case the clause آتاني.. is conjoined to the clause كنت على بيّنة.].
The clause «عمّيت عليكم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كنت على بيّنة.
The clause «أنلزمكموها» is in the position of the accusative as second mafʿūl bihi of (رأيتم).
The clause «أنتم لها كارهون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of address, the object of the verb.
(الواو) conjunction (يا قوم) like the first (لا) negating (أسأل) imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is أنا (عليه) like عليكم, attached to a ḥāl from (مالا), which is the second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (إن) a particle of negation (أجري) mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الواو) conjunction (ما) negating, acting like laysa (أنا) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun of mā (الباء) a redundant preposition (طارد) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar of mā (الذين) a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna (ملاقو) khabar of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the واو, and the nūn was dropped because of the iḍāfa (ربّهم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi, and (الميم) for the masculine plural (الواو) conjunction (لكنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for rectification (istidrāk), and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of lākinna (أرى) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is أنا (قوما) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (تجهلون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the واو is the fāʿil.
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the first vocative clause.
The clause «لا أسألكم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أن أجري ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya). [Translator's note: so in the source, «أن»; the Quranic text and the i'rab above have إن.]
The clause «ما أنا بطارد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّهم ملاقو ...» has no grammatical position: causal, giving the reason for not driving them away.
The clause «لكنّي أراكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the second causal clause, or to the conjoined answer-to-the-vocative clause ما أنا بطارد.
The clause «أراكم ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of lākinna.
The clause «تجهلون» is in the position of the accusative as naʿt of (قوما).
(الواو) conjunction (يا قوم) like the first (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (ينصر) imperfect verb, nominative, and (النون) is the nūn of protection, and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ينصر) by its implying the meaning of يمنع and يحمي ("protects, defends") (أن) a conditional particle governing the jussive [Translator's note: so in the source, «أن»; the Quranic text has إن.] (طردت) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive as protasis.. and (التاء) is the fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الهمزة) for interrogation (الفاء) conjunction (لا) negating (تذكّرون) like تجهلون, and one of the two tāʾs has been deleted for lightness.
The vocative clause «يا قوم» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the first vocative clause [Note: The repetition of the vocative (يا قوم) is to draw them on gradually (istidrāj).].
The clause «من ينصرني ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «ينصرني ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «طردتهم» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech.
The clause «تذكّرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. أتجهلون فلا تذكّرون ...
(الواو) conjunction (لا أقول) like لا أسأل (لكم) like لها, attached to (أقول), (عندي) an adverb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (خزائن) postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (الله) the Word of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) conjunction (لا أقول) like لا أسأل (إنّي) like إنّهم (ملك) khabar of inna, nominative (الواو) conjunction (لا أقول) like لا أسأل (اللام) a preposition (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (أقول) [Note: The lām is in the sense of (في), and in the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. في شأن الذين ... ("concerning those who …")], (تزدري) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ (أعين) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. تزدريهم (لن) a particle of subjunctive and negation (يؤتي) imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الله) the Word of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (خيرا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الله) the Word of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative (أعلم) khabar, nominative (الباء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [element], the ṣila of ما, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source; the wording of the phrase بما في أنفسهم appears to be abridged here.] (إنّي) like إنّهم (إذا) a particle of response, with no governing effect (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) (من الظالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of inna.
The clause «لا أقول (the first) ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause answering the first or the second vocative (لا أسألكم).
The clause «عندي خزائن ...» is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «لا أعلم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا أقول.
The clause «لا أقول (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first clause لا أقول.
The clause «إنّي ملك» is in the position of the accusative as the second maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «لا أقول (the third)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first clause لا أقول.
The clause «تزدري أعينكم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لن يؤتيهم الله ...» is in the position of the accusative as the third maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «الله أعلم ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «إنّي.. لمن الظالمين» has no grammatical position: causal.

* Morphology:
(طارد): active participle of the trilateral (طرد), its pattern being فاعل.
(تزدري): it contains the substitution (ibdāl) of the تاء by a دال; its original form is تزتري: the تاء came after the زاي and was changed into a دال, as is the case with the تاء whenever it comes after the زاي. Its pattern is تفتعل.

* Rhetoric:
Dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ», i.e. it was hidden, where the hiddenness of the proof is likened to blindness, in that each of them prevents reaching one's goals. It is also said that the speech is inverted (qalb), the original being فعميتم عنها ("you were blind to it"), as the Arabs say: أدخلت القلنسوة في رأسي ("I put the cap into my head"), and from this is the poet's saying: ترى الثور فيها يدخل الظل رأسه (You see the bull in it putting the shade into his head), and the saying of Allah the Exalted: «فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ». In these āyas there is a lofty art among the arts of badīʿ, namely combination with division (al-jamʿ maʿa al-taqsīm): that the speaker combines two or more things, then divides what he has combined. In these āyas there is a reply to the doubts they raised, when they said «ما نَراكَ إِلَّا بَشَراً مِثْلَنا وَما نَراكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ هُمْ أَراذِلُنا بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ وَما نَرى لَكُمْ عَلَيْنا مِنْ فَضْلٍ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كاذِبِينَ». So he replied to them with a reply that can be traced back to the doubts they raised, as though he were saying: if your denial of any merit in me concerns the merit of wealth and rank, I have not claimed it, nor have I told you that the treasuries of Allah are with me, so that you should dispute it with me and deny it.

* Benefits:
1- The evocative word:
In this āya comes the saying of Allah the Exalted أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوها. This word came in the context of the address of Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, to his people, when they had turned away from guidance and were determined to reject guidance and Islam. So Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, felt the extreme difficulty of conveying guidance to them — indeed its impossibility — as though you were forcing a person into something he hates and recoils from. So the word (أنلزمكموها) came: first, in its extended form, with the two pronouns, the كاف (and ها), packed into it; second, with the vowel of the mīm, which is a ḍamma, lengthened so that it became a واو; third, with the interrogative of disapproval at its beginning; and fourth, with the sound and rhythm of its letters — so that these factors combine to depict the meaning of compulsion and of trying, with extreme difficulty, to convey something to one who rejects and refuses it. Were we to put in its place أنلزمكم إياها, that sound and rhythm which it had would vanish, and the force which it conveyed would weaken. This is one of the secrets of inimitability (iʿjāz): that the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic — in its arrangement, composition, ordering and choice of words — is distinguished by a strong, pervading spirit that gives it force and vitality and distinguishes it from human speech, so that the difference between the speech of the Creator and that of the created becomes very, very great, like the difference between a deaf, lifeless statue and a living, rational, speaking human being.
2- Are the prophets superior, or the angels?
In this āya comes the saying of Allah the Exalted, on the tongue of Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace: (وَلا أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ). Some have used this āya as evidence for preferring the angels over the prophets. He said:
Because Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, said وَلا أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ; and when a person says "I do not claim such-and-such", it is fitting only if that thing is better and nobler than the states of the speaker. So since Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, said this, the angel must be better than he. The answer: Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, said this in response to their saying ما نَراكَ إِلَّا بَشَراً مِثْلَنا, since they supposed that messengers could not be from among humans but only from among the angels. So he informed them that this is a false supposition, and that the messengers to humans are only from among humans. That is why He, Glorified and Exalted, said وَلا أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ; He did not mean that the rank of the angels is higher than the rank of the prophets.

safi-cedvel:63-64.t:
* I'rab:
(قال يا قوم ... منه رحمة) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In āya (28) of this sūra.], (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (من ينصرني.. إن عصيته) the i'rab of its parallel has already been given [Note: In āya (30) of this sūra.], (الفاء) resumptive (ما) negative (تزيدون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (النون) the second one is for protection (al-wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (غير) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) (تخسير) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «the vocative: يا قوم» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أرأيتم ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «إن كنت على بيّنة» has no grammatical position; parenthetical, occurring between the verb and its object.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «آتاني منه رحمة» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the parenthetical clause.
The clause «من ينصرني ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.:
"If I disobey Allah, then who will help me against Him?"; and the implied conditional clause together with its apodosis is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition إن كنت.
The clause «the mentioned إن عصيته» has no grammatical position; explicative of the implied condition ... and the second object of the verb رأيتم is omitted, indicated by His saying: من ينصرني من الله إن عصيته, i.e. "Shall I disobey Him by abandoning what I am upon?"
The clause «ينصرني ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (من).
The clause «ما تزيدونني ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(الواو) conjunction (يا قوم) like the first (ها) particle of alerting (ذه) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (ناقة) khabar, nominative (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from آية — a naʿt (adjective) placed before the noun it qualifies — (آية) ḥāl from ناقة, its governing word being the demonstrative (الفاء) conjunction linking the effect to the cause (ذروا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is the agent (تأكل) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the reply to the request, and the agent is "it" (في أرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تأكل), (الله) the Name of Majesty, like the first (الواو) conjunction (لا) prohibitive, putting the verb in the jussive (تمسّوا) imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (بسوء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تمسّوا), (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya) (يأخذ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (عذاب) fāʿil, nominative (قريب) naʿt of عذاب, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يأخذكم..) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there be no touching of it on your part, and then a seizing of you by a punishment".
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the first clause يا قوم.
The clause «هذه ناقة الله ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «ذروها ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. "take heed, and leave her".
The clause «تأكل ...» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you leave her, she will eat".
The clause «لا تمسّوها ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ذروها.

* Morphology:
(تخسير) the regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral خسّر; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Benefits:
- The she-camel of Ṣāliḥ, upon him be blessings and peace:
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, Wahb ibn Munabbih and others among the authors of biographies (siyar) and reports mentioned that when Ṣāliḥ — upon him be blessings and peace — pressed his people with summoning, reminding and warning, they asked him to show them a sign that would confirm what he was saying. Ṣāliḥ said: "What sign do you want?" They said: "Come out with us to our festival; you will call upon your god and we will call upon our gods. If you are answered, we will follow you, and if we are answered, you will follow us." So they called upon their idols that Ṣāliḥ not be answered. Then they asked him to bring out for them from the rock a she-camel with particular fine characteristics, so that they would believe in him. He took covenants from them on that, and they agreed. Ṣāliḥ prayed two rakʿas and called upon his Lord, and the rock went into labour and brought forth a she-camel with the characteristics they had requested. The chief of the people (Jundaʿ ibn ʿAmr) and a group with him believed in him, and the rest refused out of their obstinacy and persistence. Ṣāliḥ said to them: "This she-camel has a share of drinking, and you have a share of drinking on a known day." So she would drink one day and leave it one day, and she would give them abundant milk in exchange for the water she had drunk. But the wicked among them were not pleased with that, so they conspired among themselves — they were nine persons. Qudār and his companions set off and lay in wait for the she-camel until she came back from the water; Qudār had hidden for her at the foot of a rock on her path. When the she-camel arrived, a beautiful girl urged him to hamstring her, so he attacked the she-camel with the sword and laid bare her hamstring; she gave one groan, and her calf came down from the mountain. Then Qudār stabbed her in the upper chest and slaughtered her, and the people of the town came out and divided her meat among themselves. When Ṣāliḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, learned of the matter, he said to his people: "Catch up with her calf; if you catch it, perhaps the punishment will be lifted from you."
So they went out in search of it and saw it on the mountain. Ṣāliḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, came, and when the calf saw him it wept until its tears flowed, then it groaned three times; then the rock split open and it entered it. Ṣāliḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, said to his people: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days; that is a promise not to be belied."

safi-cedvel:65-66.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction (عقروا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (الفاء) like the first (قال) past verb, and the agent is "he" (تمتّعوا) like ذروا [Note: In the previous āya (64).], (في دار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تمتّعوا) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of تمتّعوا.], and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (ثلاثة) mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) — annexed to an adverb — attached to (تمتّعوا), (أيّام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (وعد) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) (غير) naʿt (adjective) of وعد, nominative like it (مكذوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «عقروها ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"So they refused to listen to his words and hamstrung her."
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause عقروها.
The clause «تمتّعوا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ذلك وعد ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(الفاء) conjunction (لمّا جاء ... برحمة منّا) the i'rab of its parallel has already been given [Note: In āya (58) of this sūra.], (الواو) conjunction (من خزي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being نجّيناهم (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (إذ) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn is the tanwīn of compensation for an omitted clause (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (رب) the noun of inna, accusative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (هو) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) for emphasis [Note: Or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is القويّ, and the nominal clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.], (القويّ) the khabar of inna, nominative (العزيز) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «جاء أمرنا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نجّينا ...» has no grammatical position; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «the implied (نجّينا)» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the first clause نجينا.
The clause «إنّ ربّك.. القويّ» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مكذوب), passive participle of the triliteral كذب; its pattern is مفعول. It has also been said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern مفعول, like المعقول and المنضور ... etc. [Translator's note: المنضور is as printed; possibly المنظور is intended.]
(القويّ), a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the verb قوي يقوى, of the class of fariḥa; its pattern is فعيل; the yāʾ of فعيل has been assimilated (idghām) into the final radical of the word.

* Rhetoric:
The implicit, imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَعْدٌ غَيْرُ مَكْذُوبٍ», taken figuratively, as though the one making the promise said to it: "I will fulfil you." If he fulfils it, he has told it the truth; otherwise he has lied to it. So there is an implicit, imaginative metaphor. It has also been said that it is a loose metonymy (majāz mursal), taking «مكذوب» to mean "false" and "failing to come". And the hyperbole of sarcasm in calling that a "promise" is not hidden.

safi-cedvel:67-68.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (أخذ) past verb (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (ظلموا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (الصيحة) the agent of أخذ, nominative (marfūʿ) (الفاء) conjunction (أصبحوا) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — [Note: Or a complete verb, and the wāw is the agent.. and جاثمين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent.] and the wāw is the noun of aṣbaḥa (في ديار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاثمين), the khabar of aṣbaḥa [Note: Or attached to the complete verb أصبحوا.], and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (جاثمين) the khabar (predicate) of أصبحوا, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «أخذ.. الصيحة» has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: Or conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) clause in the previous āya, and what lies between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined is a parenthesis.].
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أصبحوا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(كأن) lightened from the heavy form; its noun is an omitted pronoun referring to Thamūd (لم) a particle of negation, jussive and conversion [of the tense] (يغنوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent (في) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يغنوا), (ألا إنّ ثمود ... بعدا لثمود) the i'rab of its parallel has already been given [Note: In āya (60) of this sūra.].
The clause «كأن لم يغنوا ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in the complete (أصبحوا) [Note: It may be a second khabar of the defective أصبحوا.].
The clause «لم يغنوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the lightened ka-anna.
The clause «إنّ ثمود كفروا» has no grammatical position; resumptive, carrying a causal sense.
The clause «كفروا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «(ابعدوا) بعدا..» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الصيحة), a maṣdar (verbal noun) of single occurrence (maṣdar al-marra) from the triliteral صاح يصيح; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa followed by sukūn.
(يغنوا), it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion: its original is يغناوا; when two quiescent letters met, the alif was deleted and the letter before it remained with fatḥa to indicate it; its pattern is يفعوا.

safi-cedvel:69-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (قد) particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (جاءت) past verb.. and (التاء) for the feminine (رسل) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (إبراهيم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), prevented from tanwīn because of being a proper name and foreign (بالبشرى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from رسل [Note: Or attached to (جاءت).], the sign of the genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra (قالوا) past verb and its agent (سلاما) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being نسلّم (قال) past verb, and the agent is "he", i.e. Ibrāhīm (سلام) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative [Note: What permitted beginning with an indefinite noun is that it denotes generality and is for praise. It is also possible that (سلام) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "my saying", or "my reply", or "my answer is peace".], its khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e. سلام عليكم (الفاء) conjunction (ما) negative [Note: Or it is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the interpreted maṣdar (أن جاء), i.e. "his staying was the length of his coming", that being on the omission of a muḍāf, namely "length" (مقدار).], (لبث) like قال (أن) maṣdar-forming particle (جاء) like قال (بعجل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء), (حنيذ) naʿt (adjective) of عجل, genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن جاء) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being بأن جاء — or في أن جاء — or عن أن جاء.. attached to (لبث) [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be the agent of the verb لبث, if the agent is not the pronoun referring to Ibrāhīm, i.e. "his coming was not delayed".].
The clause «جاءت رسلنا ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to an implied oath.. and the oath clause has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «(نسلّم) سلاما» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
The clause «سلام (عليكم)» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «ما لبث ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive oath clause.
The clause «جاء ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
(الفاء) conjunction (لمّا رأى) like لمّا جاء [Note: In āya (66) of this sūra.], and the agent is "he" (أيدي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (لا) negative (تصل) imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "it" (إلى) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تصل), (نكر) past verb, and the agent is "he", and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الواو) conjunction (أوجس) like نكر (من) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أوجس), (خيفة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: أوجس means "he concealed".. and al-ījās is a self-whisper or an entering [of a thought], and wajs is a passing thought.], (قالوا) like the first (لا) prohibitive, putting the verb in the jussive (تخف) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the agent is "you" (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna (أرسلنا) past verb, passive, and (نا) a pronoun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (إلى قوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أرسلنا), (لوط) إليه, genitive. [Translator's note: so printed; read "muḍāf ilayhi, genitive" — the word مضاف appears to have dropped out.]
The clause «رأى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا تصل ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from الأيدي.
The clause «نكرهم» has no grammatical position; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أوجس ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لا تخف ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «إنّا أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position; causal.
The clause «أرسلنا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (إنّ). [Translator's note: so printed; the clause is the khabar of inna.]

* Morphology:
(حنيذ), an intensive form of the active participle from حنذ يحنذ اللحم, of the class of ḍaraba, i.e. "he roasted it"; its pattern is فعيل.
(تخف), it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) to suit the jussive; its original is تخاف; when it was made jussive two quiescent letters met, so the alif was deleted because of the meeting of the two quiescent letters; its pattern is تفل. [Translator's note: so printed; the expected pattern is تفع.]
(لوط), a foreign proper name, declined as a triptote because it is a triliteral with a quiescent middle letter.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in His saying, the Exalted, «فَلَمَّا رَأى أَيْدِيَهُمْ لا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ ...» is a metonymy for their not stretching out their hands to it. And it entails that they do not eat.

* Benefits:
- The justifications for beginning with an indefinite noun:
In this āya there occurs His saying, the Exalted, قالُوا سَلاماً قالَ سَلامٌ, and in the i'rab of سلام there are two views: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "my matter is peace"; or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied as سلام عليكم; on this view the mubtadaʾ is indefinite. The basic rule is that it is not permitted to begin with an indefinite noun unless it conveys a benefit. Ibn Hishām mentioned cases in which it is permitted to begin with an indefinite noun, namely:
1- That it is described [by an adjective]: as in His saying, the Exalted, وَلَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ.
2- That it governs [another word]: (هل مسافر أخوك).
3- Conjunction, on condition that the conjoined or that to which it is conjoined is of what permits beginning with an indefinite noun, as in His saying, the Exalted, قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُها أَذىً.
4- That the khabar is an adverb or a preposition with its genitive noun, as in His saying, the Exalted, وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتابٌ. [Translator's note: two separate āyas run together as printed: وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ and لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتابٌ.]
5- That it is general, either in itself, like conditional nouns and interrogative nouns, or by something else, e.g.:
(ما رجل في الدار) and His saying, the Exalted, أَإِلهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ.
6- That what is meant by it is the reality as such: e.g. مؤمن خير من كافر.
7- That it has the meaning of a verb, as in His saying, the Exalted, وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ, which carries the meaning of imprecation.
8- That the establishment of that khabar for the indefinite noun is something extraordinary, such as: شجرة سجدت, بقرة تكلمت ...
9- That it occurs after the إذا of surprise: خرجت فإذا أسد بالباب.
10- That it occurs at the beginning of a circumstantial (ḥāl) clause, as in the poet's saying:
سرينا ونجم قد أضاء فمذ بدا ... محيّاك أخفى ضوءه كلّ شارق
(We travelled by night while a star had shone; but since your face appeared, its light has hidden every rising [star].)
The evidence: his saying ونجم قد أضاء, for نجم is an indefinite mubtadaʾ at the beginning of a ḥāl clause.
11- That the indefinite noun is for distribution (tafṣīl), as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فأقبلت زحفا على الركبتين ... فثوب نسيت وثوب أجرّ
(So I came forward crawling on my knees, one garment I forgot and one garment I trail.)

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent) (يا) a vocative particle (نوح) the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (جادلت) past verb and its fāʿil, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (الفاء) conjunction (أكثرت) like جادلت (جدال) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (ائت) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت (نا) mafʿūl bihi (الباء) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ائت), and the returning pronoun is omitted (تعد) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is أنت, and (نا) mafʿūl bihi (إن) a conditional particle governing the jussive (كنت) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (التاء) a pronoun, the noun of kāna (من الصادقين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of كنت.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause «يا نوح ...» is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «قد جادلتنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أكثرت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «ائتنا....» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: إن كنت صادقا في ما تقول فأتنا ("if you are truthful in what you say, then bring it upon us").
The clause «تعدنا» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «إن كنت من الصادقين» has no grammatical position: an explication of the implied condition [Note: Or it is a resumptive conditional clause.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: إن كنت من الصادقين فأتنا ...]..

safi-cedvel:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he" (إنّما) the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle (يأتي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (الباء) a preposition (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتي), (الله) the Word of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (إن) a conditional particle (شاء) past verb, in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is "he", and the object is omitted, i.e. شاء تعجيله لكم ("He wills to hasten it for you") (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl (ما) negating, acting like laysa (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun of mā (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, added in the khabar (predicate) (معجزين) accusative in position, genitive in form, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يأتيكم به الله» is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «إن شاء ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. فإنّ أمره إلى الله ("for its matter belongs to Allah").
The clause «ما أنتم بمعجزين» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of address in يأتيكم.
(الواو) conjunction (لا) negating (ينفع) imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (نصحي) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (إن أردت) like إن شاء.. and (التاء) is the fāʿil (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle governing the subjunctive (أنصح) imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is أنا (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أنصح), (إن كان) like كنت [Note: In the previous āya (32).], (الله) the Word of Majesty, the noun of kāna, nominative (يريد) like ينفع, and the fāʿil is "he" (أن يغوي) like أن أنصح, and (كم) mafʿūl bihi (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (ربّكم) khabar, nominative, and muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (إلى) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (ترجعون), which is an imperfect verb, passive, nominative.. and the واو is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أنصح) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أردت.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يغويكم) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يريد.
The clause «لا ينفعكم نصحي» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause يأتيكم به الله.
The clause «أردت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: فلا ينفعكم نصحي.
The clause «إن كان الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the first condition and its apodosis, i.e.: إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم فإن أردت أن أنصح لكم فلا ينفعكم نصحي [Note: In the Ḥāshiya of al-Jamal the following appears: «وجواب الشرط الثاني هو الشرط الأول وجوابه، والتقدير: وإن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم فإن أردت أن أنصح لكم فلا ينفعكم نصحي وذلك لأنه إذا اجتمع في الكلام شرطان وجواب يجعل الشرط الثاني شرطا في الأول فلا يقع الجواب إلّا إذا حصل الشرط الثاني ووجد في الخارج قبل وجود الأول لأن الشرط مقدّم على المشروط في الخارج فلو انعكس الأمر بأن وجد الأول أولا لم يقع المعلّق، فلو قال لعبده: أنت حرّ إن كلّمت زيدا إن دخلت داره لم يعتق إلّا إذا وجد دخول الدار قبل كلام زيد.. وعبارة البيضاوي هكذا تقرير الكلام: إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم فإن أردت أن أنصح لكم فلا ينفعكم نصحي» ("The apodosis of the second condition is the first condition together with its apodosis; the implied form is: and if Allah wills to lead you astray, then if I wished to advise you, my advice would not benefit you. This is because when two conditions and one apodosis come together in speech, the second condition is made a condition upon the first, so the apodosis does not occur unless the second condition is realised and exists in reality before the first exists, since a condition precedes what is conditioned upon it in reality; if the order were reversed, so that the first existed first, what is made contingent would not occur. So if someone said to his slave: 'You are free if you speak to Zayd if you enter his house', he would not be freed unless entering the house occurred before speaking to Zayd.. And al-Bayḍāwī's wording is: the purport of the speech is: if Allah wills to lead you astray, then if I wished to advise you, my advice would not benefit you"), end quote; i.e. the benefit of the advice, if the Messenger wishes it, is only complete on condition of Allah's will.].
The clause «أنصح ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أن يغويكم» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «هو ربّكم» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «ترجعون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the causal clause.

* Morphology:
(نصح): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb نصح ينصح, of the class فتح, its pattern being فعل with a ḍamma on the فاء. There are other maṣdars: نصح with a fatḥa on the نون, نصاحة with a fatḥa or a kasra on the نون, and نصاحية with a fatḥa on the نون.

* Benefits:
- One condition intervening upon another:
In this noble āya two conditions occur, namely the saying of Allah the Exalted وَلا يَنْفَعُكُمْ نُصْحِي إِنْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنْصَحَ لَكُمْ إِنْ كانَ اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُغْوِيَكُمْ هُوَ رَبُّكُمْ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ. Ibn Hishām said: this āya needs consideration, since there are not two consecutive conditions followed by an apodosis, as in the poet's saying:
إن تستغيثوا بنا إن تذعروا تجدوا ... منا معاقيل عزّ زانها كرم
(If you seek our help, if you are alarmed, you will find in us strongholds of might adorned by generosity.)

For in the noble āya no apodosis is mentioned; rather, there precedes the two conditions what is in meaning the apodosis of the first condition, so it should be supposed next to it. The original would then be: إن أردت أن أنصح لكم فلا ينفعكم نصحي إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم.
